biography.plain_text: John McCaw Jr. is an American businessman whose fortune grew from McCaw Cellular, the family telecommunications company. His father transferred a cable business to John and his brothers, who developed it into a much larger enterprise. Associated with Seattle, he later became an owner of the Vancouver Canucks and Vancouver Grizzlies.

long_biography.plain_text:
John McCaw Jr. owned the Vancouver Canucks through a period of financial strain and recovery. Improved marketing and pay-per-view television helped lift revenue, with a stronger Canadian dollar also contributing. He brought in Francesco Aquilini as an equal partner, giving the team and its arena additional capital, before selling his remaining interest to the Aquilini family.

His investment interests later reached Formula One. In 2018, he joined Lawrence Stroll's consortium in an agreement to rescue Force India from administration. The investors undertook to pay creditors and provide continuing finance for the racing operation. He also participated through his own investment company in the separate consortium backing Aston Martin's road-car business.
